text:
sam (support): Hey team — ACME reported big latency spikes and lots of 429s this morning after a traffic burst. Customer says dedicated pool didn't scale fast enough. I have a few logs attached below.

jess (sre): Thanks — can you paste the initial 429 pattern and any probe logs? Also, is this Dedicated or Private?

sam (support): Dedicated. Curl to their endpoint shows consistent 429s during the surge: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-abc123
retry-after: 10
```

maria (customer-success): Customer says they hit this around 07:12 UTC, traffic 3x normal for ~5m. They're on a reserved Dedicated instance with min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, warm_pool_size=3.

nate (platform): Ok, initial hypothesis: autoscaler created scale intents but new pods stuck in ContainerCreating/imagePullBackOff or waiting for warmchain attach. I pulled controller events: 
```
scale-controller: desired_replicas=10 current_replicas=2 pending=8
pod/ai-worker-7: ContainerCreating -> ImagePullBackOff (Failed to pull due to auth error)
attach-controller: warm-pool attach queued, IAM token rotation in-flight for account cust-acme
```

jess (sre): That imagePullBackOff + IAM rotation is a nasty combo. If pods can't pull model artifacts or the runtime image they sit pending and autoscaler thinks it's already provisioned. Can we confirm image pull error reason?

sam (support): From kubelet: "Failed to pull image "gcr.redwood/models/llm:quant-v2": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error response from daemon: pull access denied for gcr.redwood/models, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'". But the registry checks show tokens being rotated around 07:10—07:14.

nate (platform): Looks like the cluster node pool had an IAM credential refresh for the registry. Warm pool attach tries to reuse nodes but cannot pull layers while the registry rejects requests. Result: pods pending, autoscaler doesn't progress because DesiredReplica delta >0 but ReadyReplicas low.

maria (customer-success): Customer is asking for mitigation now. Any quick workaround?

jess (sre): Short-term mitigation options: 1) Increase min_replicas temporarily to force more warm pods (but won't help if image pull fails). 2) Bump warm_pool_size so more nodes are pre-attached. 3) If registry auth is the blocker, re-issue service account key or rotate tokens back. For immediate relief, we can failover traffic to a compatible hosted model variant for this customer (fallback policy) — need ops approval.

sam (support): I suggested failover to hosted small-latency variant and customer accepted for the 5m window. I've also asked infra to re-run registry token provisioning.

nate (platform): Added observation: autoscaler holdoff and probe pacing config mean we wait 12s between scale attempts and backoff increases with failures. Combined with image pull delay this produced a >2m ramp instead of expected ~30s. We should tune aggressive work: reduce scale_controller.holdoff for dedicated-tier customers in surge mode.

jess (sre): Repro steps I used locally to simulate: 
1) Set min_replicas=2, warm_pool_size=3.
2) Deploy a large traffic generator: for i in {1..300}; do curl ... & done
3) Intentionally fail image pull by pointing to private registry with expired token
Result: autoscaler increases desired, pods stuck at ContainerCreating, RPS spikes and 429s observed.

sam (support): Customer logs also show repeated attach timeouts: "attach-controller: failed to attach warm node: timeout waiting for heartbeats"

maria (customer-success): I'll update the customer: we failed over to hosted variant and are investigating root cause with platform.

nate (platform): Action items: 
- (nate) Re-run registry token provisioning for cust-acme account and confirm image pulls succeed (ETA 10m)
- (jess) Propose autoscaler config change: reduce holdoff from 12s to 4s for Dedicated surge policy and add detection to ignore pods in ImagePullBackOff when computing effective capacity (ETA PR 2d)
- (sam) Keep customer posted, confirm if the rollback of token rotation fixes it and document repro steps (ETA 15m)

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/registry-cred-rotater v2 rolled out to cluster staging at 07:25 UTC

jess (sre): Notes for postmortem: 
- Root cause: timing of registry/credential rotation + autoscaler pacing + warm_pool attach semantics. 
- Contributing: min_replicas too low for expected surge profile, autoscaler backoff too conservative for short spikes, lack of explicit signals to ignore pods blocked by image pull when judging scale progress.

sam (support): Customer confirmed we restored their flow after failover -> hosted and registry token reprovisioning — they saw latency normalize ~07:28. They've asked for a permanent fix.

maria (customer-success): Customer asks for a guaranteed golden path for future surges: recommendations?

jess (sre): Recommendations to provide to CS: 
- Increase min_replicas for customers with predictable bursts OR enable proactive warm_pool resizing on schedule. 
- Add circuit-breaker fallback to hosted variant when warm_pool attach latency > threshold. 
- Accelerate registry token TTL refresh to avoid rotation windows during expected traffic spikes. 
- Short-term: add an operator runbook for forced re-provisioning of registry creds and warm_pool attic.

nate (platform): I'll open a tracking ticket: RN-5584 "Reduce dedicated autoscaler holdoff for surge policy; ignore ImagePullBackOff pods in capacity calc" and attach logs.

sam (support): I'll keep the channel updated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
